A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SatDiFuser study, with readable text, equations, tables and figures. The supplied v1 ends after its references; v2 additionally includes Supplementary Sections 6–9. The retained material supports reliable comparison.

before.justification: Tables 1–6 report original classification, segmentation, fusion and backbone ablations, and limited-label experiments.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds learned fusion-weight results in supplementary Figure 7.

M1.justification: The DiffusionSat backbone, DDIM feature extraction, and global, localized and MoE fusion procedures remain unchanged. Supplementary diffusion equations explain the existing procedure rather than introduce a different method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same six classification and six segmentation datasets from GEO-Bench, including the same limited-label scenarios. Section 7 describes existing coverage; Figure 7 uses three already evaluated datasets.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain Satlas, SSL4EO-MAE/DINO, ScaleMAE, GFM, RemoteCLIP, CROMA, DOFA and the supervised controls. The raw-feature, concatenation and SD v2-1 backbone comparisons also remain unchanged. Added related-work citations are not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Frozen backbones, linear/UPerNet heads, metrics, reported preprocessing and the 10% labeled-data design remain unchanged. Supplementary Sections 7–8 disclose settings for existing experiments without reporting a protocol revision.

E4.justification: Section 9 and Figure 7 add a diagnostic of learned global fusion weights across scales, modules and timesteps on m-chesapeake-landcover, m-pv4ger-seg and m-NeonTree. Existing timestep, module, fusion, expert-count, backbone and data-scarcity analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The added learned-weight distributions are not uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Figure 7 adds empirical weight-allocation results for three datasets. Existing benchmark and ablation scores remain unchanged, including global fusion's 66.2 F1 on m-bigearthnet and MoE fusion's 71.6 mIoU on m-chesapeake-landcover.

T1.justification: Supplementary Section 6 adds explicit forward/reverse diffusion distributions, a cumulative-noise definition, the noise-prediction objective and DDIM reconstruction equations (5–9), absent from the supplied v1. This adds mathematical specification; the fusion equations remain unchanged and no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that generative diffusion features can support discriminative geospatial foundation models, propose the same three fusion strategies and retain the same novelty and performance claims. The abstract's wording edits do not change their scientific scope.

C2.justification: Section 6.2 explicitly explains choosing deterministic DDIM inversion over stochastic noise addition. Section 9 interprets learned weights as dataset-dependent feature selection. Existing explanations of fusion tradeoffs and limitations concerning RGB imagery and conditional models remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Sections 7–8 supply dataset splits, image and spectral properties, cross-entropy versus multilabel BCE losses, 60-versus-40-epoch schedules, and flipping/color-jitter augmentation with probability 0.5. The abstract replaces a future code-release promise with a repository link. These substantially expand reproducibility documentation without establishing changed experiments.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds five cited works covering label-efficient diffusion segmentation, COP-Gen-Beta, SatSynth, diffusion-based hyperspectral classification and diffusion autoencoders. These broaden literature coverage while retaining the existing research positioning and novelty claims.

P1.justification: The main organization and nearly all main-text prose are retained. V2 adds supplementary explanations and acknowledgements, lightly edits the abstract and captions, updates an affiliation, and provides specific supplementary cross-references.

P2.justification: V2 adds Figure 7 with three learned-weight bar charts. Figures 1–6 and Tables 1–6 preserve their displays and structure; remaining visual differences are modest text reflow, caption correction and pagination changes.

improvement.justification: V2 improves reproducibility and transparency by supplying supplementary dataset and training details missing from v1, replacing the code-release promise with a concrete link, and adding a useful weight diagnostic. These benefits outweigh minor notation problems in the new diffusion overview, notably the alpha/alpha-bar inconsistency in Equation 9. The central experimental evidence remains unchanged.
